specification.problem: Approximate the mean mu = (1/N) sum_x f(x) of a black-box function f:{0,1}^n->[0,1] using canonical amplitude estimation (the Heisenberg-limited O(1/eps) variant). The Aharonov-style phase-estimation variant and the median algorithm are only sketched or excluded.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One tiny instance: n=2 index qubits (N=4), one value qubit a, t=3 counting qubits (6 qubits total), f given as a direct rotation oracle with one query per controlled use. Excluded: variance-based rescaling for unbounded f, the Aharonov variant, the median/Durr-Hoyer algorithm, and all paper-specific details not in the abstract.

symbols.meaning: mean of f, equal to the probability of measuring a=1 after A
state-preparation unitary: Hadamards on the index register followed by the rotation oracle
number of counting qubits and the size of the counting register
integer read from the counting register, with qubit j weighted 2^j (little-endian)

equations.label: Mean as amplitude
equations.description: Uniform superposition followed by the rotation oracle, so the probability of a=1 equals the mean of f.
equations.abstract_quote: approximate the mean value of a black-box function
equations.justification: The abstract states mean estimation. The sketch's use of amplitude estimation implies this encoding; the encoding itself is not stated in the abstract.
assumptions: N is a power of two
rotation oracle with Ry(2 arcsin sqrt f(x)) controlled on x

equations.label: Grover iterate
equations.description: Q acts as a rotation by 2\theta_p in the plane spanned by the good and bad components.
equations.justification: Standard amplitude amplification, recalled from background knowledge.

equations.label: Eigenphases of Q
equations.description: A|0> is an equal-weight superposition of the two eigenvectors, so phase estimation yields \theta_p.

equations.label: Estimator
equations.description: Both y and M-y give the same estimate. The error is O(1/M) with M-1 applications of Q, hence O(1/eps) queries.
equations.justification: Standard amplitude estimation bound. The abstract only claims asymptotic optimality.

equations.label: Counting register readout
equations.description: For a counts key over the counting register only, the last character is classical bit 0. The inverse QFT must be built so that qubit j carries weight 2^j.
equations.justification: Needed to avoid the Qiskit bit-order error.
assumptions: measure counting qubit j into classical bit j

registers.name: x
registers.role: index register, Hadamard to uniform superposition

registers.name: a
registers.role: value qubit that carries sqrt(p) as the |1> amplitude

registers.name: c
registers.role: counting register for phase estimation of Q

steps.description: Apply H to every qubit of c. Prepare A|0> on x,a: H on x, then the rotation oracle onto a.
For j=0..t-1, apply controlled-Q^(2^j) with control c_j. Each Q uses A, A^-1, S_chi and S_0, so the oracle is queried twice per Q, plus once for the initial A.
Apply the inverse QFT on c, with swaps handled so that c_j has weight 2^j, then measure only c.
Compute y from the counts, take the most frequent y, and set p_hat=sin^2(pi y/M). The mean estimate is p_hat, rescaled back to the original range of f.

specification.measurement: Measure only the t counting qubits, with c_j into classical bit j.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Decode y with little-endian ordering, take the mode of y, and compute p_hat=sin^2(pi y/M). Rescale if f was rescaled.
assumptions: The tiny instance is chosen by me: n=2, t=3, an explicit f table, a direct rotation oracle.
Controlled-Q is built from the oracle placeholder, which requires a controlled version of the oracle, and each use counts as a query.
f is in [0,1] with fixed-point precision sufficient for the rotation angles.
No ancillas are needed in this version.
missing_information: The abstract does not give the paper's novel algorithm; this is the standard amplitude-estimation reconstruction.
The unbounded-variance rescaling scheme is not specified.
The Aharonov-style variant's details, including the exact phase-estimation unitary and the Hadamard test, are not specified.
The median algorithm is not specified in the abstract; the sketch's Durr-Hoyer design is unverified.
Whether the paper's algorithm avoids the QFT is unknown.
